790:       // A re-ask replaces the turn it starts from: the old question and the
791:       // answer it got are the same turn, and keeping both would read as a
792:       // conversation the reader never had.
793:       const cut = options.from
794:         ? messages.findIndex((message) => message.id === options.from)

796:       const replaced = cut >= 0 ? messages.slice(0, cut) : messages;
797: 
798:       // Files ride only on the newest turn. Re-sending megabytes of base64 with
799:       // every later question would make each turn slower than the last.
800:       const history: ChatMessage[] = [
801:         ...replaced.map((message) =>
802:           message.attachments
803:             ? {
804:                 id: message.id,
805:                 role: message.role,
806:                 content: message.content,
807:                 parts: message.parts,
808:               }
809:             : message,
810:         ),
811:         {
812:           role: "user",
813:           id: newTurnId(),
814:           content: trimmed,
815:           ...(attachments.length ? { attachments } : {}),
816:         },
817:       ];
818:       const assistantIndex = history.length;
819:       const assistantId = newTurnId();
820:       setMessages([
821:         ...history,
822:         { role: "assistant", id: assistantId, content: "", parts: [] },
823:       ]);
824:       setStreaming(true);
825:       setThinkingPhase("health_check");
826:       setOfflineReply(false);

828:       const controller = new AbortController();

831:       let content = "";

833:       let steps: RunStep[] = [];

835:       let terminal = false;
836:       let stopped = false;

838:       // Prose is appended to the open text part; a surface opens a new one, so
839:       // the transcript keeps the agent's order instead of gathering all prose
840:       // above all cards.
841:       const appendText = (text: string) => {
842:         if (!text) {
843:           return;
844:         }
845:         content += text;
846:         const last = parts[parts.length - 1];
847:         parts =
848:           last?.kind === "text"

862:             role: "assistant",
863:             id: assistantId,
864:             content,
865:             parts: [...parts],

868:             ...(failure || stopped

1: /**
2:  * The bridge between our transcript and assistant-ui's thread runtime.
3:  *
4:  * The studio owns the conversation: the sidecar writes it, memory restores it,
5:  * and every turn carries fields a generic chat message has no room for (run
6:  * steps, a failure, a stopped run, the agent's surfaces). So the runtime is fed
7:  * a mapped copy rather than being asked to hold the state: assistant-ui gets a
8:  * thread it understands, and our store keeps being the one place a turn lives.
9:  *
10:  * This module is deliberately pure — no React, no clipboard, no network — so
11:  * the mapping is testable without a DOM.
12:  */
13: 
14: import type {
15:   AppendMessage,
16:   FileMessagePart,
17:   ImageMessagePart,
18:   MessageState,
19:   ThreadMessageLike,
20: } from "@assistant-ui/react";
21: 
22: import type { ChatAttachmentPayload, ChatMessage, StudioError } from "../types";
23: import type { RunStep } from "./run";
24: 
25: /** Everything the runtime needs to know about the run that produced a turn. */
26: export interface ThreadContext {
27:   streaming: boolean;
28:   phase: string | null;
29:   offline: boolean;
30: }
31: 
32: /** What a turn carries in `metadata.custom`, read back when it renders. */
33: export interface TurnMeta {
34:   tools?: RunStep[];
35:   stopped?: boolean;
36:   error?: StudioError;
37:   retryText?: string;
38:   retryAttachments?: ChatAttachmentPayload[];
39:   phase?: string | null;
40:   offline?: boolean;
41: }
42: 
43: /** A stable id for a turn the studio creates itself. */
44: let sequence = 0;
45: export function newTurnId(): string {
46:   sequence += 1;
47:   return `turn-${sequence.toString(36)}-${Date.now().toString(36)}`;
48: }
49: 
50: export function messageIdOf(message: ChatMessage, index: number): string {
51:   return message.id ?? `turn-${index}`;
52: }
53: 
54: function isImage(mediaType: string): boolean {
55:   return mediaType.split(";")[0].trim().toLowerCase().startsWith("image/");
56: }
57: 
58: /** A stored file as a thread part the runtime can reason about. */
59: function attachmentPart(file: ChatAttachmentPayload, index: number): ImageMessagePart | FileMessagePart {
60:   if (isImage(file.media_type)) {
61:     return {
62:       type: "image",
63:       id: `file-${index}`,
64:       image: `data:${file.media_type};base64,${file.data}`,
65:       filename: file.name,
66:     };
67:   }
68:   return {
69:     type: "file",
70:     id: `file-${index}`,
71:     filename: file.name,
72:     data: file.data,
73:     mimeType: file.media_type,
74:   };
75: }
76: 
77: function contentOf(message: ChatMessage): ThreadMessageLike["content"] {
78:   if (message.role === "user") {
79:     const text = message.content ? [{ type: "text" as const, text: message.content }] : [];
80:     return [...text, ...(message.attachments ?? []).map(attachmentPart)];
81:   }
82: 
83:   if (message.role === "assistant") {
84:     if (message.parts?.length) {
85:       return message.parts.map((part) =>
86:         part.kind === "ui"
87:           ? { type: "data", name: "ui", id: part.id, data: { id: part.id, node: part.node } }
88:           : { type: "text", text: part.text },
89:       );
90:     }
91:     return message.content ? [{ type: "text", text: message.content }] : [];
92:   }
93: 
94:   return message.content;
95: }

97: function statusOf(
98:   message: ChatMessage,
99:   index: number,
100:   lastIndex: number,
101:   ctx: ThreadContext,
102: ): ThreadMessageLike["status"] {
103:   if (message.role !== "assistant") {
104:     return undefined;
105:   }
106:   if (message.stopped) {
107:     return { type: "incomplete", reason: "cancelled" };
108:   }
109:   if (message.error) {
110:     return { type: "incomplete", reason: "error" };
111:   }
112:   if (ctx.streaming && index === lastIndex) {

119:  * Our transcript as a thread the runtime can render and act on.

121:  * Only the newest turn learns the live phase and whether the model answered
122:  * from its offline guidance: an older turn is history, and history does not get
123:  * to look like it is still happening.
124:  */
125: export function toThreadMessage(
126:   message: ChatMessage,
127:   index: number,
128:   lastIndex: number,
129:   ctx: ThreadContext,
130: ): ThreadMessageLike {
131:   const isLast = index === lastIndex;
132:   const meta: TurnMeta = {

140:     ...(isLast && ctx.phase ? { phase: ctx.phase } : {}),
